Gov-MA.title: Massachusetts (Governor)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: Massachusetts — governorship; a deep-blue state Harris carried by about 25 points (61.2% to 36.0%) in 2024, though with a long tradition of electing moderate Republican governors (Weld, Cellucci, Romney, Baker).
  • Incumbent Status: Gov. Maura Healey (D), in office since January 2023, is seeking a second term with Lt. Gov. Kim Driscoll.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Democrats — Healey unopposed. Republicans — Mike Minogue 75.8%, Brian Shortsleeve 24.2% in the September 1 primary (Wikipedia, final counts; WAMC). November ballot: Maura Healey (D), Mike Minogue (R), Andrea James (independent) and Muhammed Kokonezis-Hanino (independent), per Wikipedia's race page; not checked against the Secretary of the Commonwealth's certified list as of 3 October.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Gov. Maura Healey (D) faces Mike Minogue (R), an Army veteran and former CEO of medical-device maker Abiomed who had put more than $15 million of his own money into the race by the September 1 primary (CommonWealth Beacon) and backed Trump in 2024.
  • Voting History: Healey won 63.7% to 34.6% over Geoff Diehl (R) in 2022 (+29.1), a Democratic gain; in 2018 Charlie Baker (R) was re-elected 66.6% to 33.1% over Jay Gonzalez (D) (+33.5).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: Housing and living costs are voters' top concerns, and majorities disapprove of Healey's handling of them despite 52% overall job approval (Northeast Independent / UNH). Energy costs: Minogue proposes a gas-tax holiday when prices exceed $4 a gallon and would scrap the state's Net Zero mandate and the MBTA Communities zoning law; offshore wind is a flashpoint (WAMC). State spending: Minogue calls Healey a 'tax-and-spend Democrat' and proposes a public spending dashboard.
  • National Alignment: Healey runs against the Trump administration's impact on health care and the state economy, promising to restore health funding and to remove ICE's presence in the state (NBC Boston). Minogue supported Trump in 2024 and hosted a Trump–Vance fundraiser, but campaigns on fiscal and energy issues; the Democratic Governors Association labels him a 'MAGA puppet'.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook Solid D (as of Oct 1); Inside Elections Solid D (as of Sept 17); Sabato Safe D (as of Sept 29). The UNH Survey Center (released Sept 28, likely voters) has Healey leading 54% to 38%, narrowed from 54% to 30% in its August 20–24 poll; UMass Amherst/YouGov (Aug 5–12) had Healey ahead 53% to 33%. State campaign-finance (OCPF) figures reported on September 1 showed Minogue with more than $8M cash on hand, largely self-funded, against Healey's $6.6M (CommonWealth Beacon).
  • Significance for India-US Interests: Massachusetts' Indian-American population was 125,534 (1.79%) in the 2020 Census. No India-specific position was identified in the sources reviewed as of 3 October 2026.

Gov-MD.title: Maryland (Governor)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: Maryland — governorship; a solidly Democratic state Harris carried by about 28.5 points (62.6% to 34.1%) in 2024, with a large federal workforce in the Washington suburbs that has been hit hard by Trump-era job cuts. Republicans last won the governorship with Larry Hogan in 2014 and 2018.
  • Incumbent Status: Gov. Wes Moore (D), in office since January 2023, is seeking a second term with Lt. Gov. Aruna Miller.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Democrats — Moore 88.3%, Eric Felber 11.7%; Republicans — Dan Cox 43.3%, Ed Hale 36.0%, John Myrick 6.4%, Carl Brunner 6.1%, Shannon Wright 2.4%, in the June 23 primary (Wikipedia, final counts). November ballot (certified, Maryland State Board of Elections candidate list): Wes Moore/Aruna Miller (D), Dan Cox/Rob Krop (R), Andy Ellis/Owen Silverman Andrews (Green), Cathy White/Cathy Permut (Working Class Party); write-in candidates not listed.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: A rematch of 2022: Gov. Wes Moore (D), a former nonprofit executive and author, faces former Del. Dan Cox (R), a Trump-aligned lawyer who organised buses to the 6 January 2021 rally and lost to Moore by about 32 points.
  • Voting History: Moore won 64.5% to 32.1% over Cox in 2022 (+32.4); in 2018 Larry Hogan (R) was re-elected 55.4% to 43.5% over Ben Jealous (D) (+11.9).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: Affordability and energy: Maryland electricity prices rose about 13%, prompting 2026 legislation to cap utility executive pay and speed up energy projects; Cox pledges to cut taxes, fees and electric bills (WTOP; Fox45). The structural budget deficit, which Cox blames on Moore spending the Hogan-era surplus. Moore's mid-decade congressional redistricting push stalled in the state Senate under President Bill Ferguson.
  • National Alignment: Moore frames the race around protecting Maryland from Trump administration policies, citing more than 31,000 federal workers fired in the state (over 40,000 including contractors). Cox avoids national themes — 'This is about Maryland. It's not about the national political scene' — while Democrats tie him to Trump, whose approval in Maryland was about 30% (67% disapprove) in the Zenith Research poll (July 27–Aug 3) cited below. No detailed positions found from either candidate on tariffs or the Iran war.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook Solid D (as of Oct 1); Inside Elections Solid D (as of Sept 17); Sabato Safe D (as of Sept 29). The only general-election poll found, by Zenith Research for the lobbying firm Perry Jacobson and Blended Public Affairs (July 27–Aug 3, 800 likely voters; not independent), has Moore ahead 58% to 31% (Maryland Matters). As of the August 18 report Moore had $6.5M cash on hand ($15.5M raised) to Cox's $136,092 ($241,715 raised).
  • Significance for India-US Interests: Lt. Gov. Aruna Miller, Moore's running mate, was born in Hyderabad and is the first South Asian woman elected lieutenant governor in the US; as a delegate she helped organise Gov. Martin O'Malley's 2011 trade mission to India, and she took her oath on the Bhagavad Gita (Wikipedia). Maryland's Indian-American population was 104,617 (1.69%) in the 2020 Census.

Gov-ME.title: Maine (Governor)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: Maine Governor — open seat in a Democratic-leaning state (Harris +7 in 2024) that uses ranked-choice primaries. Forecasters rate it Solid to Likely D (see Race Outlook).
  • Incumbent Status: None. Gov. Janet Mills (D), in office since 2019, is term-limited (and ran for Senate before withdrawing).
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Democrats (ranked-choice) — Pingree 56.2%, Shah 43.8% in the final round (Shah led round one with 26.9% to Pingree's 23.2%, with Troy Jackson third at 21.1%); Republicans — Charles 60.2%, Midgley 38.8% after seven rounds, in the June 9, 2026 primary. November ballot (per Wikipedia's race page; not checked against the Maine Secretary of State's certified list): Hannah Pingree (D), Bobby Charles (R) and Rick Bennett (independent); write-in candidates not listed.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Hannah Pingree (D), former Maine House speaker and director of the governor's policy office, faces Bobby Charles (R), a lawyer and former US assistant secretary of state; independent state Sen. Rick Bennett is also running.
  • Voting History: Mills beat Paul LePage 55.7% to 42.4% in 2022 (+13.3) and Shawn Moody 50.9% to 43.2% in 2018 (+7.7).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: The Canada trade dispute (75% of Mainers concerned), heating-oil and energy costs, housing, and healthcare access in rural areas.
  • National Alignment: Pingree runs on continuity with Mills on costs, healthcare and climate; Charles runs on taxes, energy and public safety; Bennett offers a centrist independent option.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook Solid D (Oct 1); Inside Elections Likely D (Aug 6); Sabato Likely D (Aug 26). A New York Times/Portland Press Herald/Siena poll (June 19–26; 608 likely voters) had Pingree 50%, Charles 36% and Bennett 8% in the three-way race, and Pingree 55% to Charles 40% head-to-head.
  • Significance for India-US Interests: Indian-American physician Dr Nirav Shah, former Maine CDC director and principal deputy director of the US CDC, led the first round of the Democratic primary before losing on ranked-choice tabulation. No India-specific position by the nominees was identified in the sources reviewed as of 3 October 2026.

Gov-MI.title: Michigan (Governor)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: Michigan Governor — open seat in a Rust Belt swing state Trump carried by 1.4 points in 2024. Rated Lean D (Cook, Sabato), Tilt D (Inside Elections).
  • Incumbent Status: None. Gov. Gretchen Whitmer (D), in office since 2019, is term-limited.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Democrats — Benson 83.2%, Swanson 16.8%; Republicans — James 50.1%, Johnson 35.2%, Cox 13.0% (withdrawn) in the August 4 primary. November ballot: Jocelyn Benson (D), John James (R) and Anthony Hudson (Libertarian), per Wikipedia; other minor-party/independent candidates not confirmed against the certified list as of 3 October.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Jocelyn Benson (D), secretary of state since 2019 and a national figure for defending the 2020 election results, faces Rep. John James (R), an Army veteran and businessman from MI-10, endorsed by Trump.
  • Voting History: Whitmer beat Tudor Dixon 54.5% to 43.9% in 2022 (+10.5) and Bill Schuette 53.3% to 43.7% in 2018 (+9.6).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: Auto jobs and the US–Canada tariff war, electricity prices and data-centre growth, roads and school funding.
  • National Alignment: Benson runs on costs, democracy and protecting Michigan jobs from trade fallout; James runs on Trump's manufacturing agenda, taxes and public safety.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook Lean D (Oct 1); Inside Elections Tilt D (Aug 6); Sabato Lean D (Aug 26). A Marist poll (Sept 24–27) has Benson 53%, James 41%; polling averages through Sept 6 (RealClearPolitics, Race to the WH) showed her ahead by 6–7 points.

Gov-MN.title: Minnesota (Governor)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: Minnesota Governor — open seat in a Democratic-leaning state (Harris +4 in 2024). Republicans have not won the governorship since 2006. Rated Solid D (Cook), Likely D (Inside Elections), Safe D (Sabato).
  • Incumbent Status: None. Gov. Tim Walz (D) withdrew in January amid a scandal over fraud in state-funded social services.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Democrats — Klobuchar 89.7%, Layne 5.8%; Republicans — Demuth 43.4%, Lindell 32.5%, Qualls 21.4% in the August 11 primary. November ballot: Amy Klobuchar (DFL), Lisa Demuth (R) and Steven Young (Green), per Wikipedia; other minor-party/independent candidates not confirmed against the certified list as of 3 October; write-in candidates not listed.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Sen. Amy Klobuchar (DFL), in the Senate since 2007 and a 2020 presidential candidate, faces Lisa Demuth (R), Speaker of the Minnesota House since 2025, who beat MyPillow's Mike Lindell. Either would be Minnesota's first woman governor.
  • Voting History: Walz beat Scott Jensen 52.3% to 44.6% in 2022 (+7.7) and Jeff Johnson 53.8% to 42.4% in 2018 (+11.4).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: Accountability for the social-services fraud scandal, federal immigration enforcement in the Twin Cities, education and the state budget.
  • National Alignment: Klobuchar runs as a pragmatic, bipartisan steward promising to clean up state agencies; Demuth runs on fraud accountability, taxes and public safety.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook Solid D (Oct 1); Inside Elections Likely D (Aug 6); Sabato Safe D (Aug 26). The RealClearPolitics average (through Sept 15) gives Klobuchar 49.4% to Demuth's 39.8%; the most recent public poll identified, by Republican firm co/efficient (Sept 14–15), had Klobuchar 47%, Demuth 45%. A Klobuchar win would also open her Senate seat to a gubernatorial appointment.

Gov-NE.title: Nebraska (Governor)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: Nebraska — governorship; a solidly Republican agricultural state that Trump carried by about 20 points (59.3% to 38.9%) in 2024, though Harris won the Omaha-based 2nd congressional district. The unicameral, officially nonpartisan legislature has a Republican majority.
  • Incumbent Status: Gov. Jim Pillen (R), a pork producer and veterinarian in office since January 2023, is seeking a second term with Lt. Gov. Joe Kelly; he was endorsed by Trump before the filing deadline.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Republicans — Pillen 75.4%, John Walz 9.6%, Sheila Korth-Focken 7.8%, Gary Rogge 3.7%; Democrats — former state Sen. Lynne Walz 91.5%, Larry Marvin 8.5%, in the May 12 primary (Wikipedia, final counts). November ballot: Jim Pillen (R) and Lynne Walz (D); third-party/independent candidates not confirmed against the certified list as of 3 October. Former Republican state Sen. Brett Lindstrom, who lost the 2022 GOP primary to Pillen, launched a nonpartisan petition bid that the Secretary of State rejected on Aug 14 after invalidating signatures, and on Sept 1 filed as the nominee of the newly formed America First Party; Rick Beard is the Legal Marijuana NOW nominee (Nebraska Examiner).

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Gov. Jim Pillen (R) faces Lynne Walz (D), a former teacher, realtor and eight-year state senator from Fremont (and 2018 running mate to Bob Krist), with conservative Brett Lindstrom also seeking a place on the ballot.
  • Voting History: Pillen won 59.2% to 36.0% over Carol Blood (D) in 2022 (+23.2); in 2018 Pete Ricketts (R) was re-elected 59.0% to 41.0% over Bob Krist (D) (+18.0).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: The budget: Walz says Nebraska has swung from a $1.2 billion surplus to a $750 million deficit after income-tax cuts, and pledges an independent waste audit; Pillen calls the crisis 'make-believe' and opposes reversing the cuts (Nebraska Public Media). Property-tax relief remains unresolved after the $170 million in offsets Pillen sought stalled in the legislature. Governance controversies: a $2.5 million no-bid state contract under Lincoln Police investigation, and Pillen's threats of primary challenges against GOP legislators (Nebraska Examiner).
  • National Alignment: Pillen runs as a Trump-endorsed conservative on income-tax cuts, gun rights (NRA-endorsed) and social policy, including a push for a six-week abortion ban. Walz pitches bipartisanship — endorsed by three former Republican state senators — promising to appoint Democrats, Republicans and independents, and to legalise medical marijuana by executive order on day one. No detailed positions found from either candidate on tariffs or the Iran war.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook Solid R (as of Oct 1); Inside Elections Solid R (as of Aug 2026); Sabato moved the race from Safe to Likely R on Sept 29. No independent public poll was identified as of 3 October; a Walz-campaign poll by the Democratic firm Lake Research (Sept 8–14) shows a 40%–40% tie, with Lindstrom 9% and Beard 4% (News Channel Nebraska). Pillen reported $9.47M cash on hand to Walz's $650,000 in the pre-primary report covering to April 27, though Walz has outraised him since.
  • Significance for India-US Interests: Nebraska's Indian-American population was 9,107 (0.46%) in the 2020 Census. No India-specific position was identified in the sources reviewed as of 3 October 2026.

Gov-NH.title: New Hampshire (Governor)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: New Hampshire Governor — a two-year term in a swing state that has voted Democratic for president since 2004 but favoured Republican governors since 2016. Forecasters rate it Likely to Solid R (see Race Outlook).
  • Incumbent Status: Kelly Ayotte (R), elected in November 2024 and sworn in in January 2025; seeking a second two-year term.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Democrats — Cinde Warmington won the September 8, 2026 primary, at which Ayotte was renominated. November ballot: Kelly Ayotte (R) and Cinde Warmington (D); third-party/independent candidates not confirmed against the certified list as of 3 October.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Kelly Ayotte (R), a former US senator and state attorney general, faces Cinde Warmington (D), a healthcare lawyer and former Executive Councilor (2021–2025) who ran for governor in 2024.
  • Voting History: In November 2024, Ayotte defeated Joyce Craig 53.6% to 44.3% (+9.3) for the open seat; Chris Sununu beat Tom Sherman 57.0% to 41.5% in 2022 (+15.5).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: Property taxes (55% back a cap on school-tax increases), the Canada trade dispute (71% disapprove of Trump's handling), housing costs and Ayotte's Medicaid record.
  • National Alignment: Ayotte runs on the state's "live free" low-tax model and border security; Warmington runs on healthcare, Medicaid and abortion rights, tying Ayotte to the Trump administration.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:

Gov-NM.title: New Mexico (Governor)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: New Mexico — governorship; a Democratic-leaning, majority-minority state that Harris carried by 6 points (51.9% to 45.9%) in 2024. The economy depends heavily on Permian Basin oil and gas revenue and federal installations, including Los Alamos and Sandia national laboratories.
  • Incumbent Status: None. Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham (D), in office since January 2019, is term-limited.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Democrats — Deb Haaland 72.3%, Sam Bregman 27.7%; Republicans — Gregg Hull 47.0%, Doug Turner 36.9%, Duke Rodriguez 16.1%, in the June 2, 2026 primary (Wikipedia, final counts). Democratic lieutenant-governor nominee Maggie Toulouse Oliver withdrew on June 18 for health reasons and was replaced by Stephanie Garcia Richard; former Las Cruces Mayor Ken Miyagishima ended his independent bid on July 17 and endorsed Hull. November ballot: Deb Haaland (D, with Stephanie Garcia Richard) and Gregg Hull (R, with David Gallegos); third-party/independent candidates not confirmed against the certified list as of 3 October.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Deb Haaland (D), former US Interior Secretary and congresswoman — the first Native American cabinet secretary — faces Gregg Hull (R), the former mayor of Rio Rancho, who runs on deregulation and rural economic growth.
  • Voting History: Lujan Grisham won 52.0% to 45.6% over Mark Ronchetti (R) in 2022 (+6.4), after defeating Steve Pearce (R) 57.2% to 42.8% in 2018 (+14.4).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: Data centres and water: Haaland pledges a day-one moratorium on new large-scale data centres pending guardrails, while Hull opposes a moratorium and favours deal-by-deal local negotiation, citing the $165 billion Project Jupiter AI campus in Doña Ana County (KUNM). Cost of living: the Haaland ticket emphasises rent regulation and protecting Medicaid and Medicare coverage; Hull's stresses cutting regulatory barriers and rural growth. No televised debate: Haaland ended negotiations on Sept 25, and KOB-TV will host Hull alone on Oct 8 (Santa Fe New Mexican).
  • National Alignment: Haaland, a former Biden cabinet member, runs on protecting federal health coverage from cuts and environmental guardrails; Hull argues her moratorium would send 'a nationwide message that New Mexico is closed for business', and his campaign says she is afraid to defend her record. No detailed positions found from either candidate on tariffs, immigration or the Iran war.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook Solid D (as of Oct 1); Inside Elections Likely D (as of Sept 17); Sabato Safe D (as of Sept 29). The Albuquerque Journal's Research & Polling Inc. survey (Aug 21–28, 516 likely voters) has Haaland ahead 49% to 43%; partisan polls range from a Democratic BSP Research poll (Jul 22–Aug 7) showing Haaland 41%–24% to a Republican McLaughlin & Associates poll (Jul 13–15) showing 46%–45%. For June 28–Sept 7, Haaland raised $3.4M and held $3.4M cash; Hull raised $943,000 with about $509,000 left (Santa Fe New Mexican).
  • Significance for India-US Interests: New Mexico's Indian-American population was 5,807 (0.27%) in the 2020 Census. No India-specific position was identified in the sources reviewed as of 3 October 2026.

Gov-NV.title: Nevada (Governor)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: Nevada Governor — a swing state Trump carried in 2024, the first Republican presidential win there since 2004. Rated Toss Up (Cook), Tilt R (Inside Elections), Leans R (Sabato) — see Race Outlook for dates.
  • Incumbent Status: Joe Lombardo (R), first term since January 2023, seeking re-election.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Republicans — Lombardo 90.8%; Democrats — Ford 63.3%, Hill 23.9% in the June 9 primary. November ballot: Joe Lombardo (R) and Aaron Ford (D); third-party/independent candidates not confirmed against the certified list as of 3 October.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Joe Lombardo (R), former Clark County sheriff, faces Aaron Ford (D), Nevada's attorney general since 2019 and the state's first Black AG.
  • Voting History: Lombardo unseated Steve Sisolak 48.8% to 47.3% in 2022 (+1.5); Sisolak had beaten Adam Laxalt 49.4% to 45.3% in 2018 (+4.1).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: The Las Vegas tourism slide, housing affordability, water and Lombardo's record vetoes against the Democratic legislature.
  • National Alignment: Lombardo runs as a pragmatic, independent-minded Republican on public safety and the economy; Ford ties him to Trump-era tariffs and cuts and runs on costs and consumer protection.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook Toss Up (Oct 1); Inside Elections Tilt R (Aug 6); Sabato Leans R (Aug 26). Polling averages updated Sept 10 (polls through Sept 8) range from Lombardo +2.7 (Decision Desk HQ) to Ford +0.5 (RealClearPolitics); Silver Bulletin has Lombardo 45.5%, Ford 44.1%. An Emerson College poll (Sept 5–8) had Ford 44%, Lombardo 42%.

Gov-NY.title: New York (Governor)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: New York — governorship; a large, Democratic-leaning state that Harris carried by 12.6 points in 2024 (55.9% to 43.3%), the biggest Republican swing of any state that year. Republicans have not won statewide since George Pataki's re-election in 2002.
  • Incumbent Status: Gov. Kathy Hochul (D), in office since August 2021 after Andrew Cuomo's resignation and elected to a full term in 2022, is running for re-election with former New York City Council Speaker Adrienne Adams as her running mate.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Both nominations were settled without a contest at the June 23 primary: Hochul and Blakeman ran uncontested. Rep. Elise Stefanik (R) withdrew on December 19, 2025, and Lt. Gov. Antonio Delgado (D) ended his primary challenge on February 10, 2026. November ballot: Kathy Hochul (D, Working Families), Bruce Blakeman (R, Conservative), Larry Sharpe (Libertarian) and Carl Gottstein (independent), per Wikipedia's race page; write-in candidates not listed; not checked against the State Board of Elections certified list as of 3 October.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Kathy Hochul (D), seeking a second full term, faces Bruce Blakeman (R), the Nassau County Executive, who is running with Todd Hood and has Donald Trump's endorsement.
  • Voting History: Hochul beat Lee Zeldin 53.1% to 46.7% in 2022 (+6.4), the closest New York governor's race since 1994; in 2018 Andrew Cuomo beat Marc Molinaro 59.6% to 36.2% (+23.4).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: The race centres on cost of living. Blakeman promises the largest income-tax cut in state history, exempting income under $100,000 for joint filers and paying for it partly with money now spent on immigrant and refugee aid; Hochul points to child tax credits and energy and property-tax rebates, and has refused to raise income or corporate taxes. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's support for Hochul is a live issue; Siena found 50% of voters think it helps her. Opposition to large data centres is also strong, at 63% statewide in the same poll.
  • National Alignment: Hochul runs against Trump: 51% of likely voters tell Siena that his endorsement of Blakeman hurts, and Trump's favourability in the state is 34–63. Blakeman is campaigning as a Trump ally (Trump is reportedly due to campaign with him in Syracuse on October 9) on taxes, public safety and immigration, where Siena finds the gap narrowest (Hochul 47–43).

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook rates the race Solid D and Inside Elections Likely D (both as of Oct 1); Sabato rates it Safe D (Sept 29). Two independent polls differ on the margin: Siena (Sept 11–17, 1,144 likely voters) has Hochul ahead 50% to 41%, while Quinnipiac (Sept 17–20, 1,026 likely voters) has her ahead 58% to 39%. In the September periodic state filing (reported Sept 29), Hochul reported $18.5M cash on hand, and the state Democratic Party a further $15M. Blakeman had $4.6M available at July 11 and qualifies for public matching funds.
  • Significance for India-US Interests: Hochul issued a proclamation for India's 80th Independence Day in August 2026 that praised the state's Indian-American community (DT Next). No India-specific position by Blakeman was identified in the sources reviewed as of 3 October 2026.

Gov-OH.title: Ohio (Governor)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: Ohio Governor — open seat in a state that has trended Republican (Trump +11 in 2024). Rated Toss Up (Cook) and Lean R (Inside Elections, Sabato) — not the Safe R in the seat sheet.
  • Incumbent Status: None. Gov. Mike DeWine (R), in office since 2019, is term-limited.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Republicans — Ramaswamy 82.4%, Putsch 17.6%; Democrats — Amy Acton unopposed in the May 5 primary. November ballot: Vivek Ramaswamy (R), Amy Acton (D) and Don Kissick (Libertarian), per Wikipedia; not confirmed against the Ohio Secretary of State's certified list as of 3 October; write-in candidates not listed.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Vivek Ramaswamy (R), billionaire founder of Roivant Sciences and 2024 presidential candidate, with Senate President Rob McColley as running mate, faces Dr Amy Acton (D), Ohio's health director during the early COVID-19 pandemic, with ex-party chair David Pepper.
  • Voting History: DeWine won 62.4% to 37.4% over Nan Whaley in 2022 (+25.0) and 50.4% to 46.7% over Richard Cordray in 2018 (+3.7).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: Cost of living, data-centre power demand, the Iran conflict and Ramaswamy's unconventional proposals — ending state income and property taxes, consolidating public universities — dominate. Ramaswamy has faced racist attacks on his Indian heritage and Hindu faith, including from his primary opponent.
  • National Alignment: Ramaswamy runs as a Trump-endorsed outsider on tax abolition, education and deregulation; Acton runs on healthcare, public schools and competent, steady leadership.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook Toss Up (Oct 1); Inside Elections Lean R (Aug 6); Sabato Lean R (Aug 26). A bipartisan Fabrizio Ward (R)/Impact Research (D) poll (June 14–16) had Acton 47%, Ramaswamy 44%. Ramaswamy held $30.7M cash on hand at the June 5 state reporting date to Acton's $8.1M; his running mate Rob McColley has called Republican complacency "the most dangerous opponent we possibly have."
  • Significance for India-US Interests: High. Ramaswamy, son of Indian immigrants from Kerala, would be Ohio's first Asian-American governor and the first Hindu governor in US history. His standing, and the identity-based attacks on him within the GOP, will be closely watched by the Indian-American community and in India.

Gov-OK.title: Oklahoma (Governor)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: Oklahoma — governorship; an open seat in a deeply Republican state that Trump carried by 34.3 points in 2024 (66.2% to 31.9%), winning every county. Oklahoma has not backed a Democrat for president since 1964.
  • Incumbent Status: None. Gov. Kevin Stitt (R), in office since January 2019, is term-limited.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Republicans — June 16 primary: Gentner Drummond 26.3%, Mike Mazzei 26.0%, Chip Keating 18.5%, Jake Merrick 14.5%, Charles McCall 11.8%. In the August 25 runoff, Mazzei beat Attorney General Drummond 50.3% to 49.7%, a margin of about 2,000 votes, and Drummond conceded. Democrats — Cyndi Munson 74.9%, Constance Johnson 22.3%, Arya Azma 2.8% on June 16, 2026. November ballot: Mike Mazzei (R) and Cyndi Munson (D); third-party/independent candidates not confirmed against the certified list as of 3 October.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Mike Mazzei (R), a former state senator and finance chairman who was later Stitt's Secretary of Budget, won the runoff with Trump's endorsement. He faces House Minority Leader Cyndi Munson (D) of Oklahoma City, the first Asian-American woman elected to the state legislature.
  • Voting History: Stitt beat Joy Hofmeister 55.4% to 41.8% in 2022 (+13.7), and beat Drew Edmondson 54.3% to 42.2% in 2018 (+12.1).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: The October 2 OETA debate (NonDoc) turned on four issues. On education, Mazzei backs school choice and rejects more money for a 'dysfunctional system', while Munson wants to put money into public schools and raise teacher pay. On the subsidised aluminium smelter planned at Inola, Mazzei cites jobs and military aluminium supply and Munson objects to a $255M public subsidy and its environmental risks. On AI data centres, Munson proposes a moratorium from day one and Mazzei supports expansion. Mazzei also wants to eliminate the state income tax.
  • National Alignment: Mazzei runs as a Trump-endorsed Republican; he pre-taped the debate so he could attend a Trump rally in Durant. Munson runs as a pragmatic, cross-party candidate, emphasising rural healthcare and Medicaid access, and tax relief for working families rather than the wealthy. Beef prices, rancher concerns and ICE arrests have also come up.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook rates the race Solid R (as of Oct 1). Inside Elections moved it from Solid R to Likely R (as of Oct 1). Sabato rates it Safe R (as of Sept 29). No independent general-election poll has been published. Mazzei has spent about $11M of his own money on the race (NonDoc, Oct 2).
  • Significance for India-US Interests: No India-specific position was identified in the sources reviewed as of 3 October 2026.

Gov-OR.title: Oregon (Governor)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: Oregon Governor — a Democratic state where governor's races have been closer than federal ones. Forecasters rate it Lean to Likely D (see Race Outlook).
  • Incumbent Status: Tina Kotek (D), first term since January 2023, seeking re-election.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Democrats — Kotek 83.6%; Republicans — Drazan 40.5%, Diehl 33.0%, Dudley 16.9% in the May 19, 2026 primary. November ballot: Tina Kotek (D) and Christine Drazan (R); third-party/independent candidates not confirmed against the certified list as of 3 October.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Tina Kotek (D), former Oregon House speaker, faces Christine Drazan (R), a state senator and former House minority leader, in Oregon's first gubernatorial rematch since 1978.
  • Voting History: Kotek beat Drazan 47.0% to 43.5% in 2022 (+3.5), with independent Betsy Johnson taking 8.6%; Kate Brown won 50.1% to 43.7% over Knute Buehler in 2018 (+6.4).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: Homelessness and housing supply, drug policy after the rollback of Measure 110, public safety in Portland, transportation funding and the gas tax.
  • National Alignment: Kotek runs on housing production and opposition to Trump-era federal actions; Drazan runs on public safety, homelessness and affordability, backed by the Farm Bureau and anti-abortion groups.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook Lean D (Oct 1); Inside Elections Lean D (Aug 6); Sabato Likely D (Aug 26). A poll by the Republican firm Public Opinion Strategies (June 22–24; client not stated) had Drazan 48%, Kotek 44%.

Gov-PA.title: Pennsylvania (Governor)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: Pennsylvania — governorship; the decisive swing state of the 2024 presidential race, which Trump carried by 1.7 points (50.4% to 48.7%) after Biden won it in 2020. Democrats hold the governorship and the state House, and Republicans the state Senate.
  • Incumbent Status: Gov. Josh Shapiro (D), in office since January 2023 and formerly the state's attorney general, is running for a second term with Lt. Gov. Austin Davis.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Both nominees ran unopposed in the May 19 primary (Wikipedia). Rep. Dan Meuser decided against a bid in July 2025 and endorsed Garrity, and Doug Mastriano said in January 2026 that he would not run. For lieutenant governor on the Republican side, Jason Richey took 65.6% to John Ventre's 34.4%. November ballot: Josh Shapiro (D), Stacy Garrity (R), Ken Krawchuk (Libertarian), Tony Dastra (Green) and Bill Messner (Constitution), per Wikipedia's race page; not checked against the Pennsylvania Department of State certified list as of 3 October.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Josh Shapiro (D), seeking a second term, faces State Treasurer Stacy Garrity (R) of Bradford County. Garrity is a retired Army Reserve colonel with Trump's endorsement.
  • Voting History: Shapiro beat Doug Mastriano 56.5% to 41.7% in 2022 (+14.8), and Tom Wolf beat Scott Wagner 57.7% to 40.7% in 2018 (+17.1).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: Data centres dominate the race (City & State PA). Garrity wants new projects paused until protective rules are in place, while Shapiro, who courted them earlier, now applies stricter standards. Garrity's 'Turnaround PA' plan offers property-tax relief for seniors and repeal of the gross-receipts tax on electricity and gas. Shapiro points to more than $3B in extra school funding and favours legalising recreational marijuana.
  • National Alignment: Shapiro has sued the Trump administration several times, defends abortion access, and runs on affordability and his cross-party appeal. Garrity is a self-described Trump ally who questioned the 2020 result, and she campaigns on tax cuts, natural gas and school choice. Trump's approval in the state is weak: 27% in Franklin & Marshall's August 17–23 poll.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook rates the race Solid D and Inside Elections Solid D (both as of Oct 1); Sabato rates it Safe D (Sept 29; moved from Likely D on Sept 3). NYT/Inquirer/Siena (Sept 15–21, 615 likely voters) has Shapiro ahead 58% to 38%, and Franklin & Marshall (Aug 17–23, registered voters) has him ahead 50% to 25%. For the June 6–Sept 14 filing period, Shapiro raised $13.3M and held $19.8M cash on hand; Garrity raised $1.8M and held $1.3M.
  • Significance for India-US Interests: No India-specific position was identified in the sources reviewed as of 3 October 2026.

Gov-RI.title: Rhode Island (Governor)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: Rhode Island — governorship; a small, heavily Democratic New England state that Harris carried by 13.8 points in 2024 (55.5% to 41.8%), the closest presidential result there since 1988. The seat is effectively open after the incumbent lost his primary.
  • Incumbent Status: Gov. Dan McKee (D), in office since March 2021 when Gina Raimondo became US Commerce Secretary, and elected to a full term in 2022. He lost the September 9 Democratic primary and is not on the November ballot.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Democrats — Helena Foulkes 62%, McKee 38% on September 9, a rematch of their 2022 primary, which Foulkes lost by about 3 points. Republicans — Aaron Guckian beat Elaine Pelino by 259 votes (about 50.6% to 49.4%); a recount requested by Pelino confirmed the result. November ballot: Helena Foulkes (D), Aaron Guckian (R) and independents Ken Block, Jay Gotra and C.D. Reynolds, per Rhode Island Current (Sept 15); not checked against the Secretary of State's certified list as of 3 October.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Helena Buonanno Foulkes (D), a former CVS Pharmacy president and later CEO of Hudson's Bay, faces Aaron Guckian (R), the 2022 Republican nominee for lieutenant governor and a former aide to Gov. Don Carcieri. Ken Block, an independent on his third run for governor, is pushing for a two-way race with Foulkes.
  • Voting History: McKee beat Ashley Kalus 57.9% to 38.9% in 2022 (+19.1). In 2018 Gina Raimondo beat Allan Fung 52.6% to 37.2% (+15.5), with independent Joe Trillo on 4.4%.

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: The closure of the Washington Bridge, shut for safety in 2023 and still causing nearly three years of congestion, and the housing crisis both drove McKee's defeat; every challenger attacks the state Department of Transportation's record. Foulkes would use revenue from the 'millionaire's tax' to fund housing construction and would bring in an outside director for the transport department. Block would remove state taxes and surcharges from energy bills.
  • National Alignment: Foulkes runs as a mainstream Democrat on affordability and reproductive rights, and opposes the Trump agenda. Guckian is the Republican standard-bearer in a state where Trump won 41.8%. Block casts himself as a non-partisan reformer and leaves reproductive-health questions to the legislature.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook rates the race Solid D and Inside Elections Solid D (both as of Oct 1); Sabato rates it Safe D (Sept 29). In independent polls before the primary, UNH (Aug 20–24, 750 likely voters) had Foulkes 40%, Block 19% and Guckian 15%, and Emerson/WPRI (Aug 21–22, 1,000 likely voters) had Foulkes 45%, Block 21% and Guckian 18%. A Block campaign poll by Opinion Diagnostics (released Sept 29) showed him ahead of Foulkes in a hypothetical two-way race. At June 30, Foulkes had $3.34M cash on hand, including an old $1.8M loan balance, against Block's $90K and Guckian's $30K. Neither Guckian nor Block qualifies for state matching funds.
  • Significance for India-US Interests: Independent candidate Jay Gotra was born in Mumbai and founded Alliance Security, a Rhode Island firm with more than 700 employees (Diya TV). No India-specific position by Foulkes, Guckian or Block was identified in the sources reviewed as of 3 October 2026.

Gov-SC.title: South Carolina (Governor)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: South Carolina — governorship; an open seat in a solidly Republican state that Trump carried by 17.9 points in 2024 (58.2% to 40.4%). Democrats have not won a governor's race there since 1998.
  • Incumbent Status: None. Gov. Henry McMaster (R), in office since January 2017, is term-limited.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Republicans — June 9 primary: Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette 28.9%, Alan Wilson 26.2%, Rep. Ralph Norman 17.1%, Rom Reddy 14.2%, Rep. Nancy Mace 12.1%. In the June 23 runoff, Wilson beat Evette 68.6% to 31.4%; Trump, who had endorsed Evette in May, endorsed both candidates the week before. Democrats — Jermaine Johnson 59.7%, Billy Webster 29.7%, Mullins McLeod 10.7% on June 9, with no runoff needed. November ballot: Alan Wilson (R), Jermaine Johnson (D), Michael Addison (United Citizens), Walid Hakim (Green); write-in candidates not listed.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Attorney General Alan Wilson (R), the longest-serving state attorney general in the country (in office since 2011), faces state Rep. Jermaine Johnson (D) of Hopkins, a former professional basketball player. Johnson is the Democrats' first Black nominee for governor in 36 years.
  • Voting History: McMaster beat Joe Cunningham 58.0% to 40.7% in 2022 (+17.4), and beat James Smith 54.0% to 45.9% in 2018 (+8.0).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: Taxes and infrastructure lead the race (WMBF). Wilson promises to eliminate the state income tax and cut property taxes, and to speed up approval of road projects. Johnson wants targeted income-tax relief for lower-income families, lower property taxes, more affordable housing, and state reinvestment in roads, bridges, vocational training and local manufacturing. The only scheduled debate is on October 6.
  • National Alignment: Wilson runs as a Trump-aligned conservative and enters the general election with Trump's (dual) endorsement. Johnson runs as an outsider on affordability and working families, after winning the primary on modest funds against self-funding rivals.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook and Inside Elections rate the race Solid R (both as of Oct 1); Sabato rates it Safe R (Sept 29). No independent general-election poll has been published. Two Democratic-aligned polls show Wilson ahead: Hart Research (Aug 12–15) 50% to 42%, and Public Policy Polling (July 16–17) 45% to 37% (Wikipedia). No current general-election fundraising totals could be confirmed.
  • Significance for India-US Interests: Rom Reddy, an Isle of Palms manufacturing businessman who grew up partly in India, his mother's home country (Post and Courier), self-funded a Republican primary bid and finished fourth with 14.2%. No India-specific position by either nominee was identified in the sources reviewed as of 3 October 2026.

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:

Gov-TN.title: Tennessee (Governor)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: Tennessee — governorship; an open seat in a deeply Republican state that Trump carried by 29.7 points in 2024 (64.2% to 34.5%). Harris won only Davidson (Nashville), Shelby (Memphis) and Haywood counties, and Republicans hold supermajorities in the legislature.
  • Incumbent Status: None. Gov. Bill Lee (R), in office since January 2019, is term-limited.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Republicans — August 6 primary: Sen. Marsha Blackburn 43.6%, Rep. John Rose 32.9%, state Rep. Monty Fritts 23.5%. Trump endorsed neither Blackburn nor Rose (Tennessee Lookout). Democrats — Jerri Green 69.0%, Carnita Atwater 17.9%, Kevin Lee McCants 5.4%, Tim Cyr 4.2%, Adam Kurtz 3.5% (Wikipedia). November ballot: Marsha Blackburn (R), Jerri Green (D), David Hatley (independent), Lauren Pinkston (independent), Robert Vick (independent); write-in candidates not listed.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: US Sen. Marsha Blackburn (R) faces Memphis City Council member Jerri Green (D), who is also interim Shelby County chief public defender, in the state's first all-woman major-party contest for governor. Independent businessman David Hatley is self-funding heavily. If Blackburn wins, she would appoint her own Senate successor.
  • Voting History: Lee beat Jason Martin 64.9% to 32.9% in 2022 (+32.0), and beat Karl Dean 59.6% to 38.6% in 2018 (+21.0).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: Green campaigns on affordability (Tennessee Lookout): Medicaid expansion for about 300,000 uninsured people, scrapping the grocery tax, using unspent TANF funds to clear medical debt, and ending state incentives for data centres and corporate rebates. Blackburn has refused all four proposed debates, calling Green a 'socialist' who would 'defund the police'.
  • National Alignment: Blackburn is a Trump-aligned China hawk whose campaign has played up being 'tough on China'. Green would end Highway Patrol cooperation with ICE and protect doctors who provide women's healthcare from prosecution under the state's abortion ban, and she models her approach on Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook and Inside Elections rate the race Solid R (both as of Oct 1); Sabato rates it Safe R (Sept 29). A TargetSmart poll for the Democratic-aligned Progress Fund PAC (Sept 9–12, 600 likely voters) has Blackburn 45%, Green 36% and Hatley 10%. Green said she had raised more than $1.5M as of late September (Tennessee Lookout, Sept 28).
  • Significance for India-US Interests: No India-specific position was identified in the sources reviewed as of 3 October 2026.

Gov-TX.title: Texas (Governor)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: Texas Governor — a Republican state (Trump +14 in 2024) where Democrats have not won the governorship since 1990.
  • Incumbent Status: Greg Abbott (R), in office since 2015, seeking a record fourth term.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Republicans — Abbott 81.8%, Chambers 11.2%; Democrats — Hinojosa 58.5%, Bell 9.8%, Villescaz 6.8% in the March 3, 2026 primary. November ballot: Greg Abbott (R), Gina Hinojosa (D) and Pat Dixon (Libertarian), per Wikipedia's race page; not confirmed against the Texas Secretary of State's certified list as of 3 October.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Greg Abbott (R), former state attorney general and architect of Operation Lone Star on the border, faces Gina Hinojosa (D), an Austin state representative since 2017 and former school-board president.
  • Voting History: Abbott beat Beto O'Rourke 54.8% to 43.9% in 2022 (+10.9) and Lupe Valdez 55.8% to 42.5% in 2018 (+13.3).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: Property taxes and school vouchers, the power grid, border security, the 2025 mid-decade redistricting and healthcare costs — the defining issue in South Texas.
  • National Alignment: Abbott runs on border enforcement, school choice and tax relief alongside Trump; Hinojosa runs on public schools, healthcare and the state's handling of floods and grid failures.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook Lean R (Oct 1, moved from Likely R); Inside Elections Likely R (Aug 6); Sabato Likely R (Aug 26). Recent polls: Marist (Sept 17–20) Hinojosa 49%, Abbott 46%; Texas Southern University (Sept 15–19) Abbott 49%, Hinojosa 45%; Emerson (Sept 12–14) Abbott 49%, Hinojosa 46%. An average of six polling aggregators (Sept 23) gave Abbott 48.1% to Hinojosa's 46.2%. Abbott reported $67.2M cash on hand to Hinojosa's $3.0M in the July 15 semiannual filing.
  • Significance for India-US Interests: No India-specific position was identified in the sources reviewed as of 3 October 2026. Texas has a large, fast-growing Indian-American community, centred in Houston and Dallas–Fort Worth.

Gov-VT.title: Vermont (Governor)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: Vermont Governor — a two-year term in one of the most Democratic states, which nonetheless keeps re-electing a moderate Republican (the "Vermont paradox"). Cook, Inside Elections and Sabato rate it Solid/Safe R; Nate Silver's Silver Bulletin model rates it a Toss-up (see Strategic Outlook).
  • Incumbent Status: Phil Scott (R), in office since 2017 and regularly ranked the most popular governor in the US, seeking a sixth term.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Republicans — Scott 98.5%; Democrats — Janoo 49.1%, Richards 46.6% (51.3% to 48.7% of the two-candidate vote, excluding write-ins) in the August 11 primary. November ballot: Phil Scott (R) and Amanda Janoo (D); third-party/independent candidates not confirmed against the certified list as of 3 October.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Phil Scott (R), a moderate who has publicly opposed Trump, faces Amanda Janoo (D), an economist endorsed by former Govs. Howard Dean and Madeleine Kunin, labour unions and environmental groups.
  • Voting History: Scott won 73.2% in 2024 and 71.0% to 23.9% over Brenda Siegel in 2022, with margins widening every cycle since 2016.

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: Property taxes and education funding reform, housing shortages, flood recovery after successive disasters, and healthcare costs.
  • National Alignment: Scott runs as a fiscally cautious, socially moderate independent voice; Janoo runs on a progressive economic agenda and argues Democrats should end Scott's long tenure.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook Solid R (as of Oct 1); Inside Elections Solid R (as of Aug 6); Sabato Safe R (as of Aug 26); Nate Silver's Silver Bulletin model rates it a Toss-up (as of Sept 25). The independent UNH Survey Center poll (Sept 17–21) has Janoo ahead 49% to 43%, after Scott led by 15 points (June 18–23) and 11 points (July 15–20) in earlier UNH polls.
  • Significance for India-US Interests: No India-specific position was identified in the sources reviewed as of 3 October 2026.

Gov-WI.title: Wisconsin (Governor)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: Wisconsin — governorship; an open seat in the closest state of the 2024 presidential race, which Trump carried by 0.9 points (49.6% to 48.7%). Democrats have held the governorship since 2019.
  • Incumbent Status: None. Gov. Tony Evers (D), in office since January 2019, announced in July 2025 that he would not seek a third term.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Democrats — August 11 primary: David Crowley 39.8%, Francesca Hong 39.4%, Kelda Roys 7.5%, Joel Brennan 4.7%; Sara Rodriguez (4.1%) and Mandela Barnes (4.1%) had withdrawn but stayed on the ballot. Crowley dropped out on July 8 and re-entered on July 18 with Evers' endorsement. Hong conceded rather than request a recount. Republicans — Tom Tiffany 95.3%, Andy Manske 4.6%. November ballot: David Crowley (D) and Tom Tiffany (R); third-party/independent candidates not confirmed against the certified list as of 3 October (primary results: Wikipedia).

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley (D), a moderate who would be Wisconsin's first Black governor, is running with Secretary of State Sarah Godlewski. He faces US Rep. Tom Tiffany (R) of rural northern Wisconsin, who has Trump's endorsement and is running with David Varnam.
  • Voting History: Evers beat Tim Michels 51.2% to 47.8% in 2022 (+3.4), and unseated Scott Walker 49.5% to 48.4% in 2018 (+1.1).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: Data centres are a defining issue (WPR), with the Microsoft site at Mount Pleasant among the projects in question. Tiffany would end all state subsidies for data centres, and Crowley wants a more rigorous review of incentives and data centres that 'pay their way'; 74% of voters say the costs outweigh the benefits (Marquette, Sept). Tiffany proposes returning the state surplus, cutting property taxes and a 10% income-tax cut for working families. Cost of living is the top issue for 45% of voters.
  • National Alignment: Tiffany is Trump-endorsed but has split with him on several issues (Newsweek): he opposes renaming Lake Ontario, opposes data-centre subsidies, and opposed the waiver of beef tariffs on behalf of Wisconsin farmers. Crowley runs against 'billionaire' money and on Trump's unpopularity in the state (38% approve, 60% disapprove), and 70% of voters oppose tariffs on Canadian goods.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook and Inside Elections rate the race Toss Up (both as of Oct 1); Sabato rates it Leans D (since Aug 12). Marquette Law School (Sept 16–23, 692 likely voters) has Crowley ahead 49% to 46%; among registered voters he leads 46% to 45%. For July 1–Sept 23, Tiffany raised $26M and held $12M cash on hand, 93% of it transferred from the state Republican Party, which is funded by Diane Hendricks and the Uihleins; Crowley raised $10.2M and held $2.8M.
  • Significance for India-US Interests: No India-specific position was identified in the sources reviewed as of 3 October 2026.

IA-01.title: Iowa District 1 (House)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: IA-1 — southeast Iowa: Davenport and the Quad Cities, Iowa City, Burlington and surrounding farm counties; one of the closest seats in the country (PVI R+4).
  • Incumbent Status: Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R), a physician and Army veteran, in Congress since 2021 and seeking a fourth term.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Republicans — Miller-Meeks 71.5%, Pautsch 28.4%; Democrats — Bohannan 81.5%, Terrell 18.5% in the June 2 primary. November ballot (Iowa Secretary of State candidate list, updated Aug 19): Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R), Christina Bohannan (D), Michael Bridgford (no party); write-in candidates not listed.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R) faces Christina Bohannan (D), a University of Iowa law professor and former state representative, in their third straight matchup; independent Michael Bridgford (no party) is also on the ballot.
  • Voting History: Miller-Meeks beat Bohannan by just 799 votes in 2024 (50.0% to 49.8%) after a 53.4% to 46.6% win in 2022 (+6.8); she first won the seat in 2020 by six votes.

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: Farm-economy strain — tariffs, fuel and fertiliser prices amid the Iran war — and federal Medicaid cuts threatening rural hospitals weigh on the district; Iowa City's university electorate boosts Democratic turnout.
  • National Alignment: Bohannan runs on healthcare costs, protecting Medicaid and Social Security, and lowering prices; Miller-Meeks defends the Republican tax-and-spending package and stresses border security, veterans and her medical background.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Ratings: Cook Toss Up (Sept 25); Inside Elections Tilt D (Oct 1); Sabato Leans D (Sept 29). A Bullfinch Group poll for the Independent Center (July 13–16, 705 LV) had Bohannan 40%, Miller-Meeks 35%, Bridgford 11%. At June 30 fundraising was level at about $7M each, with Bohannan holding more cash ($5.4M vs $4.7M).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:

IL-04.title: Illinois District 4 (House)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: IL-4 — Chicago's Southwest Side (Pilsen, Little Village, Back of the Yards) and western suburbs; a majority-Latino, heavily Democratic seat rated Solid/Safe D by all major forecasters.
  • Incumbent Status: None. Rep. Jesús "Chuy" García (D), in Congress since 2019, filed for re-election but withdrew after the filing deadline, citing health and family reasons.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Democrats — Patty Garcia ran unopposed; Republicans — Lupe Castillo ran unopposed in the March 17 primary. Two Democrats who launched independent bids in protest, Byron Sigcho-Lopez and Mayra Macías, were removed from the November ballot by the state elections board; independent Chris Getty and Ed Hershey (Working Class Party) remain on the ballot. November ballot: Patty Garcia (D), Lupe Castillo (R), Chris Getty (independent) and Ed Hershey (Working Class Party); Wikipedia also lists independent Lindsay Church, whose ballot status could not be confirmed against the certified list as of 3 October; write-in candidates not listed.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Patty Garcia (D), García's longtime chief of staff with union and progressive backing, faces Lupe Castillo (R), who has minimal campaign infrastructure, plus independent Chris Getty and Ed Hershey (Working Class Party).
  • Voting History: García won about two-thirds of the vote in both recent cycles, including 67.5% in 2024; Republicans have not been competitive here.

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: The succession itself is the story: García's late withdrawal let his chief of staff run unopposed, which critics including David Axelrod called "machine tactics." Immigration enforcement in Chicago's Latino neighbourhoods, housing and jobs are core local concerns.
  • National Alignment: Garcia runs as a progressive in García's mould — on immigrant protections, opposition to ICE operations in Chicago, labour rights and affordability; Castillo runs on the national Republican platform.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook rates the race Solid D (Sept 25); it is not on Inside Elections' or Sabato's competitive lists (i.e. safe). With Sigcho-Lopez and Macías off the ballot, the race matters mainly as a test of Chicago's progressive-machine politics.

ME-02.title: Maine District 2 (House)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: ME-2 — rural northern and western Maine, including Lewiston, Bangor and Aroostook County; one of the largest districts east of the Mississippi. Trump carried it by 9.5 points in 2024, making this open seat a top Republican pickup target.
  • Incumbent Status: None. Rep. Jared Golden (D), in Congress since 2019, announced in November 2025 that he would not seek re-election.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Democrats (ranked-choice, June 9, 2026 primary) — round one Baldacci 31.7%, Dunlap 29.1%, Wood 28.8%, Loud 10.4%; Dunlap won the final round 52.5% to 47.5%. Republicans — Paul LePage ran unopposed in the June 9, 2026 primary. November ballot: Matthew Dunlap (D) and Paul LePage (R); third-party/independent candidates not confirmed against the certified list as of 3 October.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Paul LePage (R), the combative two-term former governor (2011–2019) endorsed by Trump, faces Matthew Dunlap (D), Maine's state auditor and former long-serving secretary of state, backed by former Rep. Mike Michaud.
  • Voting History: Golden survived by under a point in 2024 against Austin Theriault despite Trump's big win here, and beat Bruce Poliquin 53.1% to 46.9% after ranked-choice tabulation in 2022 (+6.2).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: The Canada trade dispute hits this border district hardest — paper, forestry, potatoes and cross-border commerce — alongside heating-oil costs and rural hospital and job losses.
  • National Alignment: LePage runs on Trump's agenda, energy costs and his record as governor; Dunlap pitches himself as an independent-minded watchdog focused on costs, healthcare and Social Security, in the mould of Golden's crossover appeal.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook Likely R (Sept 25); Inside Elections Likely R (Oct 1); Sabato Leans R (Sept 29). A poll by the Democratic firm Impact Research (Sept 8–12) showed Dunlap and LePage tied at 49%. LePage holds a clear money edge — $2.6M raised and $1.7M cash on hand at June 30 versus Dunlap's $1.2M and $228K.
  • Significance for India-US Interests: No India-specific position was identified in the sources reviewed as of 3 October 2026.

sections.html:

sections.heading: Electoral Context

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:

MT-01.title: Montana District 1 (House)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: Montana's western district — 16 counties of western Montana, including Missoula, Bozeman, Butte and Kalispell; created when Montana regained a second seat in 2022. Trump carried it 54% to 43% in 2024 (about +11.5); Cook PVI R+5. Not redrawn for 2026. Missoula and Bozeman anchor a Democratic base offset by the rural Flathead and southwest.
  • Incumbent Status: None. Rep. Ryan Zinke (R), former Navy SEAL and Trump's first-term Interior Secretary, who held the seat since 2023, announced on March 2, 2026 that he would not seek a fourth term, citing health reasons, according to the Montana Free Press.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Republicans — Aaron Flint 50.1%, Christi Jacobsen 23.0%, Al Olszewski 20.3%, Ray Curtis 6.7%; Democrats — Sam Forstag 37.3%, Ryan Busse 33.1%, Russell Cleveland 21.7%, Matt Rains 7.9%, in the June 2 primary. November ballot (Montana Free Press election guide, updated Oct 2): Aaron Flint (R), Sam Forstag (D), Nick Sheedy (Libertarian); independent candidates not confirmed against the Secretary of State's certified list as of 3 October; write-in candidates not listed.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Aaron Flint (R), a statewide talk-radio host for 17 years and Iraq/Afghanistan veteran endorsed by Trump and Zinke, faces Sam Forstag (D), 32, a former wildland firefighter and smokejumper and Forest Service employees' union officer, endorsed by Bernie Sanders and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.
  • Voting History: Zinke won 52.3% to 44.6% over Monica Tranel (D) in 2024 (+7.7), after a closer 2022 race, 49.6% to 46.5% over Tranel (+3.1), with a Libertarian taking 3–4% each time.

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: Public lands and forestry are central: Flint promises to "cut unnecessary red tape, increase responsible timber harvests", while Forstag backs sustainable harvesting and protection of federal lands (MTFP election guide). Housing costs in Missoula, Bozeman and the Flathead are acute; both candidates would curb institutional/corporate home buying. Rural hospital funding, tariffs and data-centre development also feature in local polling.
  • National Alignment: Flint opposes War Powers limits on the Iran operations ("I would not support anything that ties the hands of our military or prevents the President from acting quickly") and runs as a Trump-endorsed conservative. Forstag calls on Congress to "stop this stupid and costly war with Iran" and shift money to housing and healthcare, and wants expanded ACA subsidies and Medicare options.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Ratings: Cook Lean R (Sept 25; moved from Likely R); Inside Elections Lean R (Oct 1); Sabato Leans R (Sept 29; moved from Likely R). The nonpartisan Montana Free Press–Rutgers Eagleton poll (Aug 27–Sept 7) had Flint 42%, Forstag 41%; NonStop Local News/American Pulse (Sept 19–24, 314 LV) had Flint 46%, Forstag 45%; a Public Policy Polling survey for The Bench, a Democratic-aligned committee (Sept 9–10), had Forstag 45%, Flint 43%. At June 30 Forstag had raised $1.3M with $550,079 on hand; Flint had raised about $1.3M with $502,000 on hand.
  • Significance for India-US Interests: No India-specific position was identified in the sources reviewed as of 3 October 2026.

NC-01.title: North Carolina District 1 (House)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: Rural north-eastern North Carolina — the northern Black Belt counties plus the Outer Banks and Albemarle–Pamlico coast. Redrawn by the Republican legislature on October 21–22, 2025 to favour Republicans. The new map moved Greene, Lenoir, Wayne and Wilson counties into NC-3 and added more conservative coastal counties, including Carteret, Craven, Dare, Beaufort, Hyde and Pamlico. Under the old lines Trump won 51% to 48% in 2024; the new seat is more Republican (Cook PVI R+5).
  • Incumbent Status: Rep. Don Davis (D), in office since January 2023, seeking a third term in the redrawn seat.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Democrats — Davis unopposed. Republicans — Laurie Buckhout 39.5%, Asa Buck 34.5%, Bobby Hanig 16.2%, Eric Rouse 5.4%, Ashley-Nicole Russell 4.4% in the March 3 primary. Buckhout cleared the 30% threshold, so there was no runoff. November ballot (certified, NC State Board of Elections candidate list of Sept 21): Don Davis (D), Laurie Buckhout (R), Tom Bailey (Libertarian); write-in candidates not listed.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: A 2024 rematch: Don Davis (D), a former Air Force officer and vice ranking member of the House Armed Services Committee, faces Trump-endorsed Laurie Buckhout (R), a retired Army colonel and cyber/electronic-warfare entrepreneur who served as acting Assistant Secretary of Defense for Cyber Policy in 2025.
  • Voting History: Under the old lines Davis beat Buckhout 49.5% to 47.8% in 2024 (+1.7), with Libertarian Tom Bailey at 2.6%. In 2022 he beat Sandy Smith 52.4% to 47.6% (+4.8). The 2026 race is on substantially redrawn, more Republican lines.

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: Farm-economy stress is central. Davis, ranking member of an Agriculture subcommittee, has pressed the administration over soybean growers and opposed expanded foreign beef imports (Sept 2026). Defence jobs, including the newly added Craven County, home to Marine Corps Air Station Cherry Point, and the Coast Guard presence at Elizabeth City, and hurricane resilience on the Outer Banks are perennial issues.
  • National Alignment: Davis campaigns as a bipartisan Democrat: he sometimes votes with Republicans on cultural issues and runs on farm and defence priorities, including 31 provisions he sponsored in the FY2027 NDAA. Buckhout runs as a Trump-endorsed national-security conservative and is backed by the AI-industry super PAC Leading the Future.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Ratings split — Cook Lean R (Sept 25), Inside Elections Tilt R (as of Oct 1; moved from Lean R on Sept 17), Sabato Toss-up (as of Sept 29). No independent polls. Only partisan polls exist: a Democratic poll by GBAO (Sept 8–11) has Davis 50%, Buckhout 43%, and a Republican poll by co/efficient (April 25–29) had them tied at 41%. At June 30, Davis had raised $4.29M with $3.57M cash on hand; Buckhout had raised $3.79M with $1.83M on hand.
  • Significance for India-US Interests: No India-specific position was identified in the sources reviewed as of 3 October 2026. The race does carry a defence-industry dimension: both candidates sit in the defence and cyber policy space, Davis on House Armed Services and Buckhout as a former DoD cyber official and electronic-warfare contractor.

NE-02.title: Nebraska District 2 (House)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: Nebraska's 2nd District — the Omaha "blue dot": all of Douglas County plus Saunders County and western Sarpy County; it also awards its own presidential elector. Harris carried it 51% to 47% in 2024 (about +4.6); Cook PVI D+3. Not redrawn for 2026. Republicans still lead in registration (about 158,700 to 144,200).
  • Incumbent Status: None. Rep. Don Bacon (R), a retired Air Force brigadier general in office since 2017, announced on June 30, 2025 that he would not seek re-election, opening one of the few Harris-won seats held by a Republican.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Democrats — Denise Powell 38.8%, State Sen. John Cavanaugh 36.4%, Crystal Rhoades 14.1%, Kishla Askins 6.0% (Powell's margin 1,347 votes after late early-ballot counting); Republicans — Brinker Harding unopposed after Brett Lindstrom withdrew, in the May 12 primary. November ballot (per Wikipedia's race page; not checked against the Secretary of State's certified list): Brinker Harding (R), Denise Powell (D), Eric Foreman (Libertarian); write-in candidates not listed.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Brinker Harding (R), an Omaha City Council member and commercial real estate agent endorsed by Trump and Bacon, faces Denise Powell (D), daughter of Chilean and Cuban immigrants and co-founder of the Women Who Run PAC, backed by EMILY's List and the New Democrat Coalition.
  • Voting History: Bacon held the seat narrowly against Tony Vargas (D) twice: 50.9% to 49.1% in 2024 (+1.9) and 51.3% to 48.7% in 2022 (+2.7).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: Affordability is the dominant issue in the Omaha suburbs, with Powell focused on prices, tariffs and restoring enhanced ACA credits and Medicaid funding (Nebraska Public Media voter guide). Harding runs on his city-council record and congressional reform — a stock-trading ban and term limits. The Democratic primary left a bitter residue (critics branded Powell "Dark Money Denise" over outside spending).
  • National Alignment: Harding opposes a citizenship pathway for those who entered illegally ("They are jumping the line"), supports military aid to Israel and confronting Iran's nuclear ambitions, and has Trump's endorsement. Powell attacks tariffs and inflation, wants enhanced ACA credits reinstated and Medicaid cuts reversed, backs broader legal immigration pathways, and urges diplomacy rather than continued conflict with Iran.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Ratings: Cook Lean D (Sept 25); Inside Elections Tilt D (Oct 1); Sabato Leans D (Sept 29) — each a Democratic gain. No independent public poll was identified as of 3 October. Q2 to June 30, Powell raised $1.05M (about $2M for the cycle) and had just under $1M on hand; Harding raised $620,000 ($1.8M cycle) with $1.04M on hand. A televised debate is scheduled for October 14.
  • Significance for India-US Interests: Retiring Rep. Don Bacon was listed as a member of the Congressional Caucus on India and Indian Americans in the 118th Congress; neither nominee is a member. No India-specific position by Harding or Powell was identified in the sources reviewed as of 3 October 2026.

NJ-07.title: New Jersey District 7 (House)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: New Jersey's 7th District — affluent, highly educated north-central New Jersey: all of Hunterdon and Warren counties and parts of Morris, Somerset, Sussex and Union. Trump carried it 50% to 48% in 2024 (about +1.2); Cook PVI EVEN. Not redrawn for 2026 (lines unchanged since the post-2020 map).
  • Incumbent Status: Rep. Thomas H. Kean Jr. (R), son of former Gov. Tom Kean, first elected in 2022; running for a third term. He was absent from Congress from March to June 2026 for medical treatment, missing more than 100 votes.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Democrats — Rebecca Bennett 45.3%, Tina Shah 20.0%, Brian Varela 19.1%, Michael Roth 15.6%; Republicans — Kean unopposed, in the June 2 primary. Megan O'Rourke withdrew from the Democratic race before the vote. November ballot: Rebecca Bennett (D), Tom Kean Jr. (R) and Seamus Patrick O'Toole (independent, 'Stop Israel's Genocide' slogan), per Wikipedia's race page; not checked against the New Jersey Division of Elections certified list as of 3 October.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Tom Kean Jr. (R) faces Rebecca Bennett (D), a first-time candidate, former Navy helicopter pilot, engineer and healthcare executive.
  • Voting History: Kean won 51.8% to 46.4% over Sue Altman (D) in 2024 (+5.4), after unseating Tom Malinowski (D) in 2022, 51.4% to 48.6% (+2.8).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: A proposed ICE detention site in Roxbury (Morris County) is contentious; Kean opposed it publicly for the first time at the September 27 debate. Electricity costs, taxes and grocery prices are top concerns; Kean's months-long absence is a recurring Democratic line of attack, and the State Firefighters' Mutual Benevolent Association switched its endorsement to Bennett in September.
  • National Alignment: Kean backs Trump's Iran operations (Iran "cannot be allowed" a nuclear weapon), treats tariffs as presidential prerogative and defends the 2025 tax law as having "jumpstarted the economy". Bennett calls for ending the Iran war, linking it to gas prices, wants Congress to limit Trump's tariff powers, says the tax law favours the wealthy at the expense of Medicaid, and backs a public healthcare option.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook Lean D (Sept 25); Inside Elections Tilt D (Oct 1); Sabato Leans D (Sept 29; moved from Toss-up on Sept 16). A StimSight Research poll (Sept 8–12, 498 LV), led by former Monmouth pollster Patrick Murray but commissioned by InsiderNJ, whose owners have donated to Bennett, has Bennett 47%, Kean 42%, with Trump approval at 42–58 in the district. At June 30 Kean had raised $4.89M and Bennett $4.27M (Bennett had spent $2.83M, much of it in the primary).
  • Significance for India-US Interests: Kean was listed as a member of the Congressional Caucus on India and Indian Americans in the 118th Congress. Indian-American ICU physician Tina Shah ran in the Democratic primary and finished second with 20.0%. No India-specific position by Bennett was identified in the sources reviewed as of 3 October 2026.

NJ-09.title: New Jersey District 9 (House)

sections.heading: Seat Overview
sections.html:
• Constituency Profile: New Jersey's 9th District — 35 municipalities in Passaic, Bergen and Hudson counties, anchored by Paterson, Passaic and Clifton; plurality-Hispanic and working-class. Trump carried it 49.2% to 48.0% in 2024 (+1.2), its first Republican presidential win on these lines, though Mikie Sherrill won it 59%–40% in the 2025 governor's race; Cook PVI D+2. Not redrawn for 2026.
  • Incumbent Status: Rep. Nellie Pou (D), a 27-year state legislator (Assembly 1997–2012, Senate 2012–2025) who replaced the late Bill Pascrell on the 2024 ballot; running for a second term.
  • Top Contenders (primary results): Republicans — Rosie Pino 51.4%, Tiffany Burress 48.6% (a 366-vote margin); Democrats — Pou unopposed, in the June 2 primary. November ballot: Nellie Pou (D) and Rosie Pino (R); Terrisa Bukovinac ('Save Our Babies') has also been reported on the ballot, but third-party/independent candidates were not confirmed against the certified list as of 3 October.

sections.heading: Electoral Context
sections.html:
• Candidate Snapshot: Freshman Nellie Pou (D), a former state Senate majority caucus chair, faces Rosemary "Rosie" Pino (R), a Clifton city councilwoman and former school board member, daughter of Ecuadorian immigrants.
  • Voting History: Pou won the open seat 50.8% to 45.9% over Billy Prempeh (R) in 2024 (+4.9). In 2022 Bill Pascrell (D) beat Prempeh 55.0% to 43.6% (+11.4).

sections.heading: Key Seat Issues
sections.html:
• Local Dynamics: Immigration enforcement weighs heavily in a plurality-Hispanic district: Pou has pressed ICE leadership in Homeland Security Committee hearings over raids near schools, churches and hospitals and filed a bill to bar agents from obscuring licence plates. The 2026 World Cup matches at MetLife Stadium were a local flashpoint, with Pino attacking FIFA over plans to sell the stadium turf. Tax cuts and affordability are Pino's core pitch.
  • National Alignment: Pou, a member of the New Democrat Coalition and Congressional Hispanic Caucus, called the renewed Iran war "illegal, unwanted, counterproductive" (July 13) and voted to reassert congressional war powers, citing rising gas prices. Pino backs "President Trump's border security policies", tax cuts for working families and full police funding, and promises patient-centred healthcare that protects pre-existing conditions.

sections.heading: Strategic Outlook
sections.html:
• Race Outlook: Cook Likely D (Sept 25); Inside Elections Likely D (Oct 1); Sabato Likely D (Sept 29). No public independent poll found. At June 30, Pou had raised $2.66M to Pino's $438,000.
  • Significance for India-US Interests: Pou's predecessor Bill Pascrell was listed as a member of the Congressional Caucus on India and Indian Americans in the 118th Congress; Pou's own membership is not verified. No India-specific position was identified in the sources reviewed as of 3 October 2026.
